VIII.}}</noinclude>him, See thou tel no body: but goe, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Leu. 14, 2.''}}* shevv thy self to the {{sup|‖}} priest, & offer the {{sup|‖}} gift vvhich Moyses commaunded for a testimonie to them.

{{verse|chapter=8|verse=5}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text={{sc|The Gospel}} vpon the thursday after Ashwensday. And also in Masse for the sicke. · Lu. 7, 1.}}And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Lu. 7, 1.''}}* vvhen he vvas entred into Capharnaum, there came to him a Centurion, beseeching him, {{verse|chapter=8|verse=6}}† & saying, Lord my boy lieth at home sicke of the palsey, & is sore tormēted. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=7}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} sayth to him, I vvil come, & cure him. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=8}}† And the Centurion making ansvver, sayd, Lord I am {{sup|‖}} not worthie that thou shouldest enter vnder my roofe: but only say the vvord, and my boy shal be healed. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=9}}† For I also am a man subiect to authoritie, hauing vnder me souldiars: and I say to this, goe, and he goeth: and to an other, come, & he cometh: and to my seruant, doe this, & he doeth it. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=10}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} hearing this, marueiled: and sayd to them that folovved him, Amen I say to you, I haue not found so great faith in Israel. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=11}}† And I say to you, that many shal come from the East and West, and shal sitte dovvne vvith Abraham & Isaac & Iacob in the kingdom of heauen: {{verse|chapter=8|verse=12}}† but the children of the kingdom shal be cast out into the exteriour darkenesse: there shal be vveeping & gnashing of teeth. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=13}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} said to the Centurion, Goe: and as thou hast beleeued, be it done to thee. And the boy vvas healed in the same houre.⊣

{{verse|chapter=8|verse=14}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mr. 1, 29. Lu. 4, 38.''}}* when {{sc|Iesvs}} was come into Peters house, he savv {{sup|‖}} his vviues mother layde, & in a fitte of a feuer: {{verse|chapter=8|verse=15}}† and he touched her hand, and the feuer left her, and she arose, and ministred to him. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=16}}† And vvhen euening vvas come, they brought to him many that had diuels: and he cast out the spirites vvith a word: and al that vvere il at ease he cured: {{verse|chapter=8|verse=17}}† that it might be fulfilled vvich vvas spoken by Esay the Prophete saying, ''He tooke our infirmities, and bare our diseases''.{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Esa. 53, 4. 1. Pet. 2, 24.''}}

{{verse|chapter=8|verse=18}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} seeing great multitudes about him, commaunded to goe beyond the vvater. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=19}}† And a {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Lu. 9, 57.''}}* certaine Scribe came, and sayd to him, Master, I vvil folovv thee vvithersoeuer thou shalt goe. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=20}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} sayth to him, the foxes haue holes, and the foules of the ayre nestes: but the sonne of man hath not vvhere to lay his head. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=21}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Luc. 9, 59.''}}* an other of his Disciples sayd to him, Lord, permit me first to goe & burie my father. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=22}}† But {{sc|Iesvs}} sayd to him, Folovv me, and {{sup|‖}} let the dead burie their dead.

{{verse|chapter=8|verse=23}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel on the 4. Sunday after the Epiphanie.}}And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mar. 4, 36. Lu. 8, 22.''}}* vvhen he entered into the boate, his Disciples folowed him: {{verse|chapter=8|verse=24}}† and loe a great tempest arose in the sea, so<noinclude>{{rh|||that}}</noinclude>
